findings.text: The helper's worker_launched_after_manifest=False branch is never taken — all four tests pass True (lines 149, 171, 190, 211) — so a predicate that always answers True still passes the file and the goal's third clause, a run whose live worker started before its manifest keeps today's classification, is unguarded.

The control log is named only as a nested `log:` key inside the `negative_control:` block; parse_manifest does not promote it to `negative_control_log`, so promotion raises for a missing declared control log (reproduced by calling the check against the delivered manifest).

The log's first line does not repeat the declared mutation string verbatim and the log records no `EXIT=` line, so even with a path supplied the control is inadmissible and the mutation's red result cannot be read by the promotion gate.

The two gate arms are recorded as prose and the armed-only `baseline_suite`/`after_suite` fields the done-when names are absent, so the review read path and the promotion suite-delta read this run's gate as unmeasured rather than as the measured zero it is.

promotion_checks.delivered_manifest: run 'r-20260929T141906421295-a-resumed-run-counts-as-working' writes a check (tests/test_a_resumed_run_counts_as_working.py) and declares the mutation 'classify from the manifest status alone, ignoring the live worker launch time' in its negative_control field, but its manifest carries no negative_control_log path. Promotion refuses a passing gate whose negative control was never run: keep the log that mutation produced beside the passing one and name its path in the manifest as `negative_control_log: <path>`
promotion_checks.with_log_path_supplied: run 'r-20260929T141906421295-a-resumed-run-counts-as-working' declares the mutation 'classify from the manifest status alone, ignoring the live worker launch time' but the log at '/tmp/negative_control.log' shows no failed control run: it records no EXIT status, so whether its run failed is unknown. A control is admitted on its facts alone — a non-zero exit record and at least one failing test id the head arm does not fail, falling back to the baseline's failing ids only when the manifest records no readable head arm — and neither fact is inferred from the log's wording or from a bare failing count. Re-run the declared mutation and keep the log it produced, with the capture's EXIT=<n> record and the runner's own list of which tests failed, or use --waive-negative-control REASON to record why the control may be accepted without it
